Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the first page of an onboarding document for a new backend engineer joining a payments team. Around 200 words.

Welcome to the payments team. This document covers what you need to know in your first two weeks — the rest lives in the runbooks linked at the end.

Payments touches money, so the review bar is higher here than on most teams. Every change to the charge or refund path needs two approvers, one of whom must be a payments team member. Don't merge around this, even for a one-line fix.

Start by reading the ledger service code before you write any. The ledger is the source of truth for every transaction; the API layer and the reconciliation jobs both read from it, and they must agree. If you change how a field is written, check both consumers.

You'll work mostly in Go, with Postgres as the primary store and Kafka for events between services. Local setup instructions are in the repo README. Run the full integration suite before your first PR, not just unit tests. It catches most of the mistakes new engineers make around idempotency keys.

Your first task will be a small bug fix, assigned by your manager after your 1:1. Use it to learn the deploy process: staging first, a canary at 5% of traffic, then full rollout. Ask your onboarding buddy before you touch anything in production.

Add a section on who to ask for what.

Who to ask

Ledger schema changes: ask the ledger service owners before you touch a migration. They know which downstream jobs read each column.

Deploy or rollback questions: your onboarding buddy for the first two weeks, then on-call after that. Check the on-call schedule in PagerDuty.

Access requests, for Postgres or the payments AWS account: your manager. These take a day or two to provision, so ask early.

PCI or compliance questions, like what you can log or store: the security team's #payments-security Slack channel. Don't guess on this one.

Questions about a specific charge or refund path: check the runbooks first. If the runbook doesn't cover it, ask in #payments-eng.

On-call rotation

Payments on-call runs weekly, handed off Monday mornings. Check the schedule and swap requests in PagerDuty. Your first on-call shift comes after your first 30 days, shadowing a rotation before you take one solo. If you page someone off-hours for a payments issue, post in #payments-eng on Discord as well, so the rest of the team has context by morning.
